concept_panel.title: Data System Trade-offs
concept_panel.explanation: Data-system architecture is about choosing explicit trade-offs under known constraints. Reliability, scalability, maintainability, operability, latency, and throughput all pull in different directions. Cloud services, self-hosting, serverless, and microservices shift who owns operational complexity. Strong answers define the workload and guarantee before naming a tool.
key_takeaways: Start with workload and guarantees.
Every architecture choice moves complexity somewhere.
Systems of record need stronger protection than derived data.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can make architectural trade-offs explicit.
concept_panel.practical_example: A cache can improve latency but creates invalidation and stale-read questions.
